items.claim: The koh-amar onset the row rests on is asserted without any original-language quotation of the formula, without naming its mouth or its written medium, and with a single-site spelling change of one of the two names inside the span left undisclosed.
items.evidence: The onset device the row argues from carries no original-language quotation anywhere in the row (all 3 pointed runs in it re-collated; none contains the formula). MT 29:21 does open verse-initially with the full title stack, כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.29.21, byte), and that stack is a member of the 32-verse object I re-swept independently (sweep: 32 verses book-wide; MT 29:21 and MT 29:25 are the two members inside this range) - but the row's own pointed run begins at the addressee phrase after the formula, so the frame form carrying the claimed seam role is quoted in the other witness alone. Ownership and medium are likewise unnamed: the formula stands inside the written communication whose contents oshb:Jer.29.1 introduces, and 29:21's own second-person plural forms, לָכֶ֛ם and לְעֵינֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.29.21, byte), bind it to that audience; neither the mouth nor the written medium is stated, which is the live question in this stretch. A single-site name-form change inside the span is undisclosed and is load-bearing on the row's own rejected alternative, which rests on the two verses being bound by those names: the name is spelled אַחְאָ֤ב (oshb:Jer.29.21, byte) and one verse later וּכְאֶחָ֔ב (oshb:Jer.29.22, byte) - the fuller spelling stands in 1 verse and the shorter base in 1 verse (skeleton substring sweeps, finals-normalized: 1 verse each, book-wide), so this is not a stray pointing difference. The royal name in the same verse IS disclosed by family and is correct (skeleton sweeps: resh-family spelling 29 verses; nun-family spelling 6 verses, including oshb:Jer.29.1 and oshb:Jer.29.3), which makes the omission an asymmetry rather than an oversight class. One paseq seg also stands at MT 29:21 inside the span (single-witness, seg layer, count-only) and is not disclosed, while the parashah marks in the span are. Confirmed correct: SAMEKH at MT 29:20 and MT 29:23; the ketiv/qere at MT 29:23 - both the unpointed and the pointed run there re-collate at byte tier against that verse; and the exegesis note at MT 29:23 correctly held as single-witness apparatus rather than text bytes. The declared heuristic disposition on the word 'continuous' is confirmed as a keyword false positive in itself, but the sentence carrying it holds the undisclosed name-form defect above.

items.claim: The full title-stack formula standing verse-initially at MT 29:25 inside this span is neither quoted nor declared, so the unit is classed from the embedded quoted letter rather than from the divine formula that owns it.
items.evidence: The span's own governing frame is neither quoted nor declared. MT 29:25, inside the row's span, opens verse-initially with כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר (oshb:Jer.29.25, byte) - the second member inside this range of the 32-verse full title-stack object I re-swept independently (sweep: 32 verses book-wide). That formula governs the quoted rival material at MT 29:26-28, so the ownership runs divine formula over embedded letter, not the reverse; the row carries no speech-formula signal at all and does not quote the formula, which leaves the one question this stretch actually turns on unanswered. The medium is also flattened: MT 29:25 charges the sending of סְפָרִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.29.25, byte), a plural, while MT 29:29 speaks of one document; the row's account uses a single letter throughout. And the claimed onset verse opens with a conjunctive form, וְאֶל (oshb:Jer.29.24, byte), joining it to the address just closed - a byte-true joiner sitting exactly on the row's own front seam, undisclosed. Confirmed correct: the pointed runs at MT 29:24 and MT 29:29 re-collate at byte tier; the gentilic at MT 29:27, הָֽעֲנְּתֹתִ֑י (oshb:Jer.29.27, byte), is the defective spelling the bytes carry and is correctly disclosed as such rather than normalized; SAMEKH at MT 29:23 and PE at MT 29:29 match the inventory under their own types; and the span carries no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note, consistent with the row's silence on both.

items.claim: The verse-initial word-event formula at MT 29:30, its shape assignment, its ordinal within chapters 27 through 29, and every parashah and paseq claim in the span all verify on the bytes and the inventories.
items.evidence: The onset holds on the bytes and the one digit the row rests on is exact. MT 29:30 opens וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ (oshb:Jer.29.30, byte), verse-initial, and belongs to the narrative word-event shape, not to the prose-sermon superscription shape or the topical-header shape; my independent sweep reproduces that object at 21 verses with 20 verse-initial and the single non-initial site outside this range, and inside chapters 27 through 29 it stands in exactly 2 verses, MT 28:12 and MT 29:30 (sweep: 2 verses), so the ordinal is right and the shape is not blended. Every mark and seg claim is exact against the inventory: PE at MT 29:29 at the front seam, SAMEKH at MT 29:32 at the close, and two paseq segs at MT 29:32 (single-witness, seg layer, count-only, no intra-verse position asserted) - the doubled-seg count is correct, and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span. Held but not fatal: MT 29:31 carries its own koh-amar naming the same figure, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל שְׁמַעְיָ֖ה הַנֶּחֱלָמִ֑י (oshb:Jer.29.31, byte), under the sending imperative שְׁלַ֤ח (oshb:Jer.29.31, byte), so two of the span's three verses head speech-formula material, and the second of them is quoted while the first is not; and the comparison to the earlier word-event verse is argued in prose without any citation for it. Neither touches the seam, which the bytes support.

items.claim: The stated warrant that nothing between the header and the closing rubric reopens the address with a new addressee or a discourse imperative is contradicted by MT 30:2, which the row quotes itself.
items.evidence: The frame verse and the closing rubric verify, but the warrant offered for holding the four verses together fails on bytes the row itself quotes. MT 30:2 carries a fresh formula, כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Jer.30.2, byte), and a command form with a second-person addressee, כְּתָב לְךָ֗ (oshb:Jer.30.2, byte); the superscription at MT 30:1 addresses no one in the second person, so the address is opened, not merely continued, at 30:2. The other witness reads the same form as a command, “Write all the words that I have spoken to you in a book.” (web:Jer.30.2), so the asserted absence of any new addressee or discourse imperative between the header and the rubric fails in both witnesses; the seam itself is unaffected, but the stated ground for it is not the ground the bytes give. Confirmed correct, and notably so: MT 30:1 carries the el-form of the prose-sermon superscription, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.30.1, byte) - an aleph-lamed member of the 11-verse object, correctly kept apart from the one-site variant elsewhere in the book that reads a different preposition; and MT 30:2's formula is the God-of-Israel shape WITHOUT the armies element, so the row is right not to declare it as the full title stack (independent sweep: the 32-verse full-stack object does not include MT 30:2). PE at MT 30:3 inside the span and SAMEKH at MT 29:32 at the front seam match the inventory under their own types, the petuchah is correctly disclosed as texture rather than warrant, and no paseq seg or ketiv/qere note falls in the span. The declared heuristic disposition on the word 'first' is confirmed as a keyword false positive, though the descriptor it sits in leans on modern poetry-line layout, which carries no boundary weight either way.

items.claim: The declared false-positive disposition is refuted: MT 30:8 carries the span's first second-person singular addressee, so the asserted absence of an addressee change at that turn is byte-false in both witnesses.
items.evidence: The declared heuristic disposition on the rejected alternative is REFUTED on the bytes of the very verse the row quotes in full. MT 30:8 carries צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ and וּמוֹסְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ (oshb:Jer.30.8, byte), second-person singular suffixed forms, where MT 30:5-7 carry none: MT 30:5 has the first-person plural שָׁמָ֑עְנוּ (oshb:Jer.30.5, byte), MT 30:6 the second-person plural commands שַׁאֲלוּ נָ֣א וּרְא֔וּ (oshb:Jer.30.6, byte), and MT 30:7 the third-person לְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Jer.30.7, byte). The other witness turns to direct address at the same verse, “that I will break his yoke from off your neck, and will burst your bonds.” (web:Jer.30.8). So the assertion that no addressee change marks that turn - and that the tsevaot stack in the verse is all that stands there - is false in both witnesses; the turn is marked, and the row's own onset criteria would reach it. The same second-person plural commands at MT 30:6 are a discourse device standing inside the span with no signal declared for them. Confirmed correct, and strongly: the interjection at MT 30:7, ה֗וֹי כִּ֥י גָד֛וֹל הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא (oshb:Jer.30.7, byte), is an exclamation over the day itself and not a woe onset against a named party, matching the book-wide role split (bare-token sweep: 7 verses, 8 tokens); the Jacob spellings at MT 30:7 and twice at MT 30:10 are defective as claimed; the postpositive stack at MT 30:8 is byte-present and correctly treated as closure corroboration rather than an onset; and every mark and seg claim is exact - nothing at MT 30:4, SAMEKH at MT 30:9, PE at MT 30:11, one paseq seg each at MT 30:8 and MT 30:11, no ketiv/qere in the span. One minor parity gap: the pointed run given for 30:5 includes the formula while the paired other-witness run omits its rendering.

items.claim: The declared false-positive disposition is refuted: the exclusivity-shaped claim that nothing divides the complaint from the reversal carries no sweep and is contested by the verse-initial pivot particle at MT 30:16 inside the span.
items.evidence: The declared heuristic disposition on the rejected alternative is REFUTED. The sentence asserts an absence - that no fresh formula divides the complaint from the reversal - and carries no sweep behind it, while the bytes put a verse-initial pivot particle at exactly that joint: MT 30:16 opens לָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Jer.30.16, byte). That token stands in 55 verses book-wide, and within chapters 29 through 31 it stands verse-initially in exactly 2 (token-bound sweep, finals-normalized: 2 verses), MT 29:32 and MT 30:16 - and at MT 29:32 the same particle heads a fresh commissioned sentence, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.29.32, byte). An exclusivity-shaped claim of this kind is not dampened by a tier label; it needs its own digit-bearing sweep naming the object, none is given, and the counterexample sits inside the row's own span. Confirmed correct: the feminine-singular addressee onset at MT 30:12 is byte-real - לְשִׁבְרֵ֑ךְ and מַכָּתֵֽךְ (oshb:Jer.30.12, byte), the suffix distinct in the pointing from the masculine form - and the chain holds unbroken to the close; PE at MT 30:11 at the front seam, SAMEKH at MT 30:17 at the close, and one paseq seg at MT 30:15 all match the inventory, with no ketiv/qere note in the span. One minor parity gap: at 30:17 the pointed run covers the whole verse while the paired other-witness run covers its closing clause alone, so the healing clause the argument turns on is not covered by the paired run the row gives.

items.claim: The covenant formula at MT 30:22 arrives on a second-person switch the row explicitly denies, and the wrath coda at MT 30:23-24 is an undisclosed consonantal near-twin of MT 23:19-20.
items.evidence: Two byte facts inside the span run against the row's own account. First, the covenant formula arrives on a person switch the row denies: across all 4 verses MT 30:18-21 the pronominal and verbal forms are third-person - יַֽעֲק֔וֹב and וּמִשְׁכְּנֹתָ֖יו (oshb:Jer.30.18, byte), בָנָיו֙, וַעֲדָת֖וֹ and לֹחֲצָֽיו (oshb:Jer.30.20, byte), אַדִּיר֜וֹ (oshb:Jer.30.21, byte), all third-person - while MT 30:22 opens וִהְיִ֥יתֶם and carries לָכֶ֖ם (oshb:Jer.30.22, byte), second-person plural; the other witness turns the same way, “You shall be my people, and I will be your God.” (web:Jer.30.22). Second, the wrath coda is an undisclosed near-twin of material outside this span: the opening run of MT 30:23, הִנֵּ֣ה סַעֲרַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה, and its closing run, עַ֛ל רֹ֥אשׁ רְשָׁעִ֖ים יָחֽוּל (oshb:Jer.30.23, byte), each stand consonantally in exactly 2 verses book-wide, MT 23:19 and MT 30:23; and מְזִמּ֣וֹת לִבּ֑וֹ together with בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִ֖ים תִּתְבּ֥וֹנְנוּ (oshb:Jer.30.24, byte) likewise stand consonantally in exactly 2 verses, MT 23:20 and MT 30:24 (skeleton sweeps, finals-normalized: 2 verses each). The pointed witnesses diverge at מִתְגּוֹרֵ֑ר (oshb:Jer.30.23, byte) against מִתְחוֹלֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.23.19, byte), the extra חֲרוֹן֙ (oshb:Jer.30.24, byte), and the extra closing בִּינָֽה (oshb:Jer.23.20, byte). A recurrence of that size bears directly on whether the coda is integral to the tents oracle or floats, and the row treats it as continuous speech without disclosing it. Third and lesser: the spelling contrast the row argues from rests on two verses outside its own span, MT 30:7 and MT 30:10, neither of which appears in the row's boundary evidence list. Confirmed correct: the plene form at MT 30:18, יַֽעֲק֔וֹב (oshb:Jer.30.18, byte), carries the extra vav before the final letter exactly as claimed and is swept per its own attested form; SAMEKH at MT 30:17, MT 30:22 and MT 31:1, and one paseq seg each at MT 30:18 and MT 30:23, match the inventory exactly, with no ketiv/qere in the span; and the frontier flag with reduced confidence on the held 31:1 attachment is the right calibration for a genuinely open seam.

items.claim: The declared false-positive disposition is refuted: MT 31:2 has no addressee at all and MT 31:3 both reports the deity in the third person and opens a feminine-singular address, so the asserted single continuous voice addressed to one figure is byte-false.
items.evidence: The declared heuristic disposition on the rejected alternative is REFUTED; the bytes contest both halves of it. Across MT 31:2 all forms referring to its subject are third-person - מָצָ֥א, לְהַרְגִּיע֖וֹ and יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.31.2, byte) - with no second-person form in the verse, so there is no figure addressed at that verse for the next one to keep addressing. MT 31:3 then opens מֵרָח֕וֹק יְהוָ֖ה נִרְאָ֣ה לִ֑י (oshb:Jer.31.3, byte), naming the deity in the third person beside a first-person singular indirect object, which cannot be the divine speaker's own voice; the other witness reads it the same way, “Yahweh appeared of old to me, saying,” (web:Jer.31.3). After that clause the feminine-singular forms begin - אֲהַבְתִּ֔יךְ and מְשַׁכְתִּ֥יךְ (oshb:Jer.31.3, byte) - continuing at MT 31:4 with אֶבְנֵךְ֙, תַּעְדִּ֣י and תֻפַּ֔יִךְ (oshb:Jer.31.4, byte). That is the same feminine-singular pointing that the bytes carry at MT 30:12, לְשִׁבְרֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Jer.30.12, byte), where it is treated as an onset warrant; here the identical criterion is denied, and 'one continuous voice addressed to the same figure' does not survive either witness. Confirmed correct: the onset formula at MT 31:2, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.31.2, byte); the following onset at MT 31:7, כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.31.7, byte); and SAMEKH at MT 31:1 at the front seam with PE at MT 31:6 at the close, no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere in the span - all exact against the inventory. One minor parity gap: the pointed run given for 31:3 covers the whole verse while its paired other-witness run drops the opening clause, which is precisely the clause carrying the voice shift.
